title: PlayStation Portable
wiki_lead:
The PlayStation Portable (PSP) is a handheld game console developed and marketed by Sony Computer Entertainment. It was first released in Japan on December 12, 2004, in North America on March 24, 2005, and in PAL regions on September 1, 2005. It is the first handheld installment in the PlayStation line of consoles. As a seventh generation console, the PSP primarily competed with the Nintendo DS.
Development of the PSP was announced during E3 2003, and the console was unveiled at a Sony press conference on May 11, 2004. The system was the most powerful portable video game console at the time of its introduction, and was the first viable competitor to Nintendo's handheld consoles after many challengers such as Nokia's N-Gage and Sega's Game Gear had failed or underperformed. The PSP's advanced graphics capabilities made it a popular mobile entertainment device, which could connect to the PlayStation 3, select PlayStation 2 games, any computer with a USB interface, other PSP systems, and the Internet. The PSP also had a vast array of multimedia features such as video playback and audio playback, leading some to classify it as a portable media player. The PSP is the only handheld video game console to use an optical disc format, the Universal Media Disc, as its primary storage medium, and the format was used to distribute both games and media content.
The PSP was received positively by critics. The system sold over 80 million units during its ten-year lifetime, making it the best selling handheld video game console of all time not made by Nintendo. Several models of the console were released, including the PSP Street and the PSP Go. The system would go on to be succeeded by the PlayStation Vita, released in Japan in December 2011, which would have backward compatibility with PSP games that were released on the PlayStation Network through the PlayStation Store. Hardware shipments of the PSP ended worldwide in 2014.

History


Pre-release
Prior to 2004, Sony was a leading company in the development and production of portable media players, producing product lines such as the Walkman for audio playback and the Watchman for live television. However, the handheld video game market would be largely dominated by Nintendo beginning with the Game Boy in 1989, with it and its successors outselling competition such as Sega's Game Gear and Bandai's WonderSwan line by significant margins. With the exception of the PocketStation in 1999, a PlayStation Memory Card capable of playing rudimentary games installed onto it, Sony would not make any attempts to enter into this market until into the sixth generation of video game consoles.
Sony Computer Entertainment first announced development of the PlayStation Portable at a press conference preceding E3 2003. Sony released extensive technical details and introduced the Universal Media Disc to be used for games, but did not show any hardware aside from that. grok_lead: The PlayStation Portable (PSP) is a handheld video game console developed and marketed by Sony Computer Entertainment as the first portable entry in the PlayStation brand. It was initially released in Japan on December 12, 2004, followed by North America on March 24, 2005, and other regions shortly thereafter, featuring a 4.3-inch widescreen TFT LCD display with 480 Ã 272 resolution capable of rendering 16.77 million colors, a MIPS-based CPU clocked up to 333 MHz, and 32 MB of main memory. The device utilized proprietary Universal Media Discs (UMD) for game distribution and supported multimedia playback of video, audio, and photos, positioning it as an early portable media player alongside gaming capabilities that rivaled home consoles of the era. Over its production run from 2004 to 2014, multiple revised models including slimmer variants and the PSP Go, which lacked a UMD drive, were introduced, with cumulative worldwide sales exceeding 76 million units by the early 2010s, reflecting its commercial success despite challenges like short battery life and widespread software piracy.
